title: Canada-resident NRI trapped using a fake ID, demand of 50 thousand dollars, Ghaziabad police's big action against a sextortion gang

reading.body:
This is an impersonation case in which a fake social media profile was used to make contact with a target, and a video call was used to capture compromising footage. The AI element sits at the threat stage rather than the contact stage: AI-generated obscene videos were allegedly held alongside the recorded footage as additional material for coercion. The system was not deployed to produce a false statement of fact or to make a decision, so the relevant failure mode is the synthetic fabrication of intimate imagery for use as leverage.

The point of failure was the absence of any check between the creation of the material and its use against a named person. Nothing in the reporting describes a platform-side or intermediary control that would have intercepted the fake profile, the recorded call, or the generated videos before the demand was made. Catching this would have required either detection of the fabricated profile at the point of account creation or identification of the synthetic media before it was used as a threat, and the reporting does not establish that either was attempted.

What is established is that four people were arrested, an FIR was registered under the BNS and IT Act, and the accused's number was linked to 40 complaints on the NCRB portal. What is not established is guilt: an arrest is not a conviction, and the allegations of extortion and of AI-generated video have not been tested in court. The reporting also does not establish who produced the AI videos or with what tool.

summary:
A Jamia Millia Islamia student named Md Faisal and three associates from Muzaffarnagar were arrested in Ghaziabad for allegedly extorting a Canada-based NRI. Police said the gang created a fake Facebook profile, recorded the victim in a compromising position during a video call on September 10, then demanded $50,000, about Rs 4.7 crore, and threatened to circulate the footage along with AI-generated obscene videos. The victim contacted the cybercrime team on September 17, and the accused's mobile number was linked to 40 cyber fraud complaints on the NCRB portal.

Police registered an FIR under the BNS and IT Act and arrested four gang members on Friday, while some associates, including Maroof, remain absconding. Investigators said the gang had been active since 2023, used mule accounts bought for Rs 15,000 each, and cheated hundreds of people in India and abroad. Their phones revealed links to at least 130 bank accounts holding Rs 6.6 crore, and AI sextortion videos were found on their devices.
